content: This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. It is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine if you should use additional reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load assessments, T-cell counts, triglyceride/cholesterol levels, and blood sugar monitoring. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the capsules in the refrigerator, away from light, and do not freeze them. If necessary, the capsules can also be stored at room temperature, but they must be discarded after 30 days. Tablets should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing any medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs.
